steps.title: Gold feels safe
steps.body: In India, many families buy gold for weddings and festivals. They often see gold as safe money. Over many decades, gold has kept its value well. But gold pays no interest. You gain only when the price goes up.

steps.title: Gold can fall for years
steps.body: The gold price can move a lot. This is called [[volatility]]. In 2011, the price reached a high. By 2015, it was about 40% lower. This kind of fall from a high is a [[drawdown]]. The price went above the 2011 high again only in 2020.

steps.prompt: After a fall, the price must rise by more than it fell to get back. Move the slider to a loss of 40%, like gold from 2011 to 2015.

output.label: Rise needed to get back to the start

steps.prompt: The chart shows the average gold price each year, in US dollars for one ounce. What does it show?
options: The price fell for some years before it rose again
The price stayed about the same
steps.explanation: The price fell from 2012 to 2015. It rose again from 2019. Gold can go up over a long time, but it does not go up every year.

chart.caption: Average gold price per year, in US dollars per ounce. Rounded.

steps.prompt: True or false: gold pays you interest while you keep it.
steps.explanation: False. Gold pays no interest. You gain only if you sell it for more than you paid.

steps.prompt: Why do some people keep a small part of their money in gold?
options: Gold often moves differently from shares, so it spreads the risk
steps.explanation: Gold often does not move in the same way as shares. When you hold different things, one bad year hurts less. This is [[diversification]].

steps.title: Where your money is
steps.body: You have **{totalAssets}** in your accounts here. **{largestPlaceShare}** of it is in **{largestPlaceName}**. Gold would be one more place for money. It pays no interest, and its price can move a lot.

steps.prompt: Imagine part of your money is in gold. Gold falls by 40%, and the rest of your money does not change. Move the gold share to see the change of all your money.

worldMove.label: Change in the rest of your money

goal.hint: Try a gold share of 25% or less.

steps.note: This is an example, not a forecast.
